correctness.rationale: Uniform ordered compositions have exactly binom(n-1,r-1) equiprobable r-part realizations. The bounded-composition recurrence and cut-subset enumeration agree for all n<=9, and all binom(n,k)^2 minors for k<=3 are checked with integer determinants. For n>=10, r=2,3,4 counts are explicitly enumerated by unique-max reasoning and the odd double-max correction, giving determinant -6(q^2-5q+2) for n=2q and -12(q-4)(q-1) for n=2q+1, each negative for q>=5. The actual standalone verify.py ran successfully; 10<=n<=300 checks are sanity checks, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact conditional longest-run enumeration is classical and not claimed as new. Malandro, Philippou--Makri, and Finch give counts or moments, while the directly read closest public result gives first-order stochastic monotonicity. These do not explicitly state the exact order-three positivity threshold; the all-n even/odd determinant obstruction and complete small-n cutoff are separately established. Priority remains conditional on historical implicit coverage.
residual_risks: An older paper on longest-run conditional distributions or total positivity may imply the evaluated determinant boundary without explicitly naming it.
The nonnegative part for n<=9 is established by fully exhaustive finite integer computation rather than a short closed symbolic inequality for every minor.

value.rationale: This is the sharp complete all-size boundary for third-order total nonnegativity of a natural conditional distribution kernel. The r=2,3,4 obstruction is not an arbitrary isolated numeric counterexample: explicit parity-dependent formulas prove it persists for every n>=10, while every smaller matrix is exhaustively certified. It distinguishes stochastic-order dependence from higher-order variation-diminishing structure relevant to run maxima and uniform compositions; no general downstream theorem is required.
